style: Clean, confident chapter-marker beat. Purple/black brand family (shared-lead-problem, speed-wins-the-job): League Gothic display headline in bright purple/white over a deep purple-black radial gradient, Montserrat wide-tracked eyebrow label. Motion is a quick punchy slam-in, a clear 2s hold, quick fade-out. Not busy — one dominant motif (the headline itself).
font: League Gothic + Montserrat (Google Fonts, matches sibling purple pieces)

customize.note: Reuse search run: `npx hyperframes catalog --query "section divider chapter marker title card slam" --json` returned motion-primitive components (headline-slam, titlecard-calm, caption-kinetic-slam) but no pre-built block combining a progress eyebrow + wrapping headline + native-CSS rule the way this template needs across 6 reused variants with differing word counts. Hand-authored per kinetic-type module, using the headline-slam / titlecard-calm / glow vocabulary as reference rather than reinventing physics. Search-miss will be reported via `npx hyperframes feedback --search-miss`.

scenes.emotion: confident, punchy, deliberate pause between chapters
scenes.motion: bg-fill + eyebrow fade/slide in -> eyebrow rule scaleX in -> whole-headline scale_punch slam-in (single unit, not per-word, so future title swaps never need span/timing edits) -> brief glow pulse landing accent -> ~2.1s clean hold -> single fade-out of the whole card ending exactly at data-duration (no hard cut, no blank frame)

template_notes.reusable_for: 6 section-divider cards total; only text content changes per reuse (no CSS/layout/timing edits needed)

find_replace_targets.#headline (text node): "PROFESSIONAL CONTENT & BRANDING" -> next title, any length from ~7 to ~32 chars

template_notes.why_whole_line_not_per_word: Per-word spans would require adding/removing <span> elements and re-tuning stagger timings for every title with a different word count. A single text node with one whole-line GSAP tween keeps every future swap a pure string replace.
template_notes.long_title_handling: Headline uses a fixed, tuned font-size (validated against the longest expected title) with max-width + text-wrap:balance so a 2-line wrap is centered and even; short titles (e.g. 'Website') simply render on one line at the same size, no per-title tuning.
